questions.scenario: It's June 29, 1976, and you stand in Victoria's central square as the Union Jack is lowered for the last time. James Mancham has just been sworn in as the Seychelles' first president.
questions.prompt: What happens to Mancham's government within the next year?
questions.butterflyEffect: In June 1977, while Mancham was in London for a Commonwealth conference, his prime minister France-Albert René seized power in a coup backed by Tanzanian-trained fighters. René's Seychelles People's Progressive Front ruled as a one-party socialist state until multiparty elections were restored in 1993.

choices.text: He is overthrown in a coup while abroad, and one-party rule follows
He wins a landslide re-election and stays in power for two decades
He voluntarily hands power to a UN-appointed transitional council
He negotiates a return to British protectorate status

questions.scenario: It's June 29, 1613, and you're in the packed galleries of the Globe watching Shakespeare's new play Henry VIII. A stage cannon fires to salute the king's entrance, and sparks catch in the thatched roof above you.
questions.prompt: What happens next?
questions.butterflyEffect: The Globe burned to the ground in under an hour; remarkably, the only recorded injury was a man whose breeches caught fire, put out with a bottle of ale. Shakespeare's company rebuilt it with a tiled roof by June 1614, and the new Globe operated until Puritan authorities closed London's theatres in 1642.

choices.text: The fire is doused quickly by attendants with buckets, no real damage done
The thatch roof catches fully and the entire theatre burns to the ground within an hour
The play continues uninterrupted while stagehands quietly extinguish the blaze
The audience riots, blaming the actors for the mishap

questions.scenario: It's June 29, 1971, and you are one of three cosmonauts preparing your Soyuz 11 capsule for re-entry after three weeks aboard Salyut 1. As you undock and begin the descent sequence, a pressure equalization valve opens early.
questions.prompt: What happens to the crew during re-entry?
questions.butterflyEffect: Georgy Dobrovolsky, Vladislav Volkov, and Viktor Patsayev died from asphyxiation when the capsule lost pressure; they remain the only humans known to have died in space. The Soviet space program grounded Soyuz for over two years, redesigned the capsule for two crew members instead of three, and made wearing pressure suits during launch and re-entry mandatory.

choices.text: They seal the valve manually and land safely
The cabin depressurizes and all three cosmonauts die before landing
They eject in emergency capsules and parachute to safety
Ground control aborts re-entry and they return to the station

questions.prompt: What happens as you near the end of the flight?
questions.butterflyEffect: Lieutenants Lester Maitland and Albert Hegenberger landed safely at Wheeler Field after a 25-hour flight from Oakland, proving long-range aerial navigation over open ocean was possible. Their radio-beacon navigation technique became a model for later transpacific routes, helping justify Hawaii's growing strategic importance to American air power.

choices.text: You run out of fuel and are forced to ditch near the islands
You successfully land at Wheeler Field, completing the first transpacific flight to Hawaii
Poor radio signals force you to turn back to California
You are intercepted and escorted in by Navy ships

questions.butterflyEffect: The collision, which killed all 83 people aboard both aircraft and remains Indiana's deadliest aviation disaster, spurred the FAA to expand mandatory transponder requirements and enlarge controlled airspace around major airports. It became a landmark case for the push toward better separation of small aircraft and commercial airliners.

choices.text: The FAA expands controlled airspace and pushes mandatory transponder use
All private aircraft are banned from national airspace
Airlines switch entirely to propeller aircraft for regional routes
Air traffic control is abolished in favor of pilot self-reporting

questions.scenario: It is just after 2 a.m. on September 9, 1954, in Orléansville, French Algeria, and the ground beneath the town is convulsing violently, toppling masonry buildings built without any thought to seismic risk.
questions.prompt: What should authorities do in the aftermath to protect the region from future quakes?
questions.butterflyEffect: The earthquake devastated Orléansville and led French colonial and later Algerian authorities to overhaul building codes, moving toward genuine seismic-resistant construction standards. Algeria has continued updating these regulations in the decades since, as the region remains prone to major earthquakes.

choices.text: Introduce and enforce modern seismic-resistant building codes
Rebuild exactly as before using traditional masonry
Abandon the town site entirely and forbid resettlement
Rely on prayer and religious observance instead of construction changes

questions.scenario: It is September 1892, and you are peering through the great 36-inch refractor at Lick Observatory on Mount Hamilton, studying the glow of Jupiter, when you notice a faint point of light close to the planet that no star catalog accounts for.
questions.prompt: What should you do to confirm whether this faint object is a new moon of Jupiter?
questions.butterflyEffect: Edward Emerson Barnard tracked the object over several nights and confirmed it was a new moon, later named Amalthea. It was the first moon discovered by direct visual observation since Galileo found Jupiter's four largest moons in 1610, and remains the last major moon found this way before photographic and later methods took over.

choices.text: Track its position over several nights to determine if it orbits Jupiter
Dismiss it as a flaw in the telescope's optics
Announce it immediately as a new planet without further observation
Assume it is a passing comet and take no further notes

questions.scenario: You served with the 442nd Regimental Combat Team in Italy in 1944, decorated with a Distinguished Service Cross for valor under fire. Decades later, you learn the Pentagon has reviewed WWII records and found the medal you received was capped by racial bias.
questions.prompt: What does President Clinton do on 21 June 2000 to correct this?
questions.butterflyEffect: Clinton upgraded 22 Asian American WWII veterans, including future Senator Daniel Inouye, from lesser decorations to the Medal of Honor. The ceremony formally acknowledged decades of discrimination against Japanese American soldiers and cemented the 100th/442nd's legacy as the most decorated unit of its size in US military history.

choices.text: He awards 22 Asian American veterans the Medal of Honor after a bias review of their records
He orders a new law lowering the threshold for the Medal of Honor
He signs a bill waiving the statute of limitations on military honors
He responds to a class-action lawsuit filed by veterans' families

questions.scenario: It is 21 June 1919 in Winnipeg. You stand with thousands of strikers on Main Street as a silent parade turns tense, and mounted police begin advancing on the crowd.
questions.prompt: What happens as the Royal North-West Mounted Police charge the strikers?
questions.butterflyEffect: The clash, remembered as Bloody Saturday, left two strikers dead and dozens injured as police and federal troops broke up the crowd. Strike leaders were arrested and the general strike collapsed days later, but the episode became a founding legend of Canadian labour politics, shaping figures like J.S. Woodsworth who later helped found the CCF.

choices.text: Strikers scatter under the charge and two men are killed, dozens more injured
The crowd overwhelms the police and forces immediate concessions
The mayor personally halts the charge before anyone is hurt
Strike leaders negotiate a truce with police on the spot

questions.scenario: You are an engineer at the University of Manchester on 21 June 1948, watching Frederic Williams, Tom Kilburn, and Geoff Tootill attempt to run a program on their new machine, the Small-Scale Experimental Machine.
questions.prompt: What historic milestone does the machine achieve moments later?
questions.butterflyEffect: The Baby successfully ran a stored program to find the highest factor of a number, proving that instructions and data could share the same electronic memory, the core idea behind nearly all modern computers. The success led directly to the commercial Ferranti Mark 1 and cemented Manchester's place at the birth of computer science.

choices.text: It executes a stored program from memory, the first machine ever to do so
It calculates pi to a record number of digits
It successfully breaks a wartime Enigma-coded message
It links electronically to a second computer for the first time

questions.scenario: It is 21 June 1921 in Knockcroghery, County Roscommon. British forces have moved into the village in reprisal for IRA activity, and you watch soldiers set fire to the shops and houses along the main street.
questions.prompt: What happens to the village that night?
questions.butterflyEffect: Most of Knockcroghery was burned to the ground, one of many reprisal burnings carried out by British forces during the war. Coming just weeks before the July 1921 truce, such reprisals intensified public revulsion at British tactics and hardened support for Irish independence.

choices.text: Most of the village's buildings are destroyed by fire
The IRA repels the soldiers before any damage is done
Local priests negotiate a halt before the fires are lit
The RIC intervenes to stop the burning and rebuilds the homes

questions.scenario: It is 21 June 1957 in Ottawa. You are a newly elected Progressive Conservative MP for Hamilton West as Prime Minister John Diefenbaker forms his first cabinet.
questions.prompt: What historic first are you about to achieve when sworn in?
questions.butterflyEffect: Ellen Fairclough became the first woman to serve in the Canadian federal cabinet. She later served as Minister of Citizenship and Immigration, where she pushed reforms reducing racial discrimination in immigration policy, and her appointment opened the door for later generations of women in Canadian federal politics.

choices.text: You become the first woman appointed to the federal cabinet
You become the first woman elected to the House of Commons
You become the first woman appointed to the Senate
You become the first woman to lead a federal political party

questions.scenario: It is September 1839 off Kowloon, and you command a British warship whose crew has been cut off from food and fresh water after Commissioner Lin Zexu banned local merchants from supplying British ships. A line of armed Chinese war junks now blocks your boats from the shore.
questions.prompt: How do you respond to the junks blocking your ships' food supply?
questions.butterflyEffect: British ships opened fire on the Chinese junks in what became known as the Battle of Kowloon, one of the first armed clashes of the conflict. The skirmish helped push both sides toward full-scale war in 1840, which ended with the Treaty of Nanking and the cession of Hong Kong to Britain.

choices.text: Open fire on the junks to force them aside
Sail back to Macau and wait for orders from London
Offer to pay the Chinese officials for safe passage
Abandon the ships and march the crew overland

questions.prompt: Who do you send up as the pinch hitter with the game on the line?
questions.butterflyEffect: Manager Art Howe sent up Scott Hatteberg, who hit a walk-off home run to complete the comeback and give Oakland its 20th consecutive win, an AL record. The game became the climactic scene of the book and film "Moneyball," cementing the streak as the public face of sabermetric roster-building, even though Oakland lost the next night to end the run.

choices.text: Scott Hatteberg
Jeremy Giambi
Ramon Hernandez
Terrence Long

questions.scenario: You are a NASA mission planner in 1977 charting Voyager 1's route through the outer Solar System. You can only choose one close flyby target beyond Jupiter and Saturn, since the spacecraft's trajectory can't reach both.
questions.prompt: Which body do you prioritize for the close flyby: Titan or Pluto?
questions.butterflyEffect: NASA chose to send Voyager 1 past Saturn's moon Titan because it was known to have a substantial atmosphere worth studying closely. That choice ruled out a Pluto flyby for both Voyager probes, leaving Pluto unvisited by spacecraft until New Horizons arrived in 2015, decades after Voyager 1 became the first craft to reach interstellar space in 2012.

choices.text: Titan, for its thick atmosphere
Pluto, to reach it before any other mission
Neither, to save fuel for a return trip
Uranus, for a longer gravity-assist path

questions.scenario: It is September 5, 1774, in Philadelphia. You are a delegate representing your colony at a gathering convened after Parliament passed the so-called Intolerable Acts punishing Massachusetts for the Boston Tea Party.
questions.prompt: What should this new colonial congress do about the Intolerable Acts?
questions.butterflyEffect: The delegates, meeting as the First Continental Congress, went on to organize a colony-wide boycott of British goods and issue a statement of grievances to the Crown. The gathering set the precedent for coordinated colonial resistance that led to the Second Continental Congress and, within two years, the Declaration of Independence.

choices.text: Coordinate a unified colonial response, including a boycott of British goods
Immediately declare independence from Britain
Petition only for lower tea taxes and disband
Raise a joint colonial army to march on Boston

questions.scenario: You are the co-pilot of Mandala Airlines Flight 091, running through the final checklist before departure from Medan on the morning of September 5, 2005, with a full passenger load bound for Jakarta.
questions.prompt: What configuration must be verified before the takeoff roll begins?
questions.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the Boeing 737 took off without its flaps and slats properly extended, causing it to stall and crash into a residential area seconds after liftoff, killing 149 people including bystanders on the ground. The disaster intensified international scrutiny of Indonesian carrier safety, contributing to the European Union's 2007 ban on Indonesian airlines from its airspace.

choices.text: Flaps and slats extended for takeoff
Cabin lighting dimmed for taxi
Autopilot engaged before brake release
Overhead bins double-checked by cabin crew

questions.scenario: It is early September 1996, and you are an emergency management official in coastal North Carolina as Hurricane Fran strengthens into a 120 mph Category 3 storm bearing down on Cape Fear.
questions.prompt: What do you order for coastal residents as the hurricane approaches?
questions.butterflyEffect: Officials ordered mandatory evacuations of coastal North Carolina before Fran made landfall near Cape Fear on September 5, 1996. The storm caused roughly $5 billion in damage and severe inland flooding as far as Raleigh, but the evacuations are credited with keeping the death toll far lower than the destruction would otherwise have caused.

choices.text: Order mandatory evacuation of coastal areas
Leave evacuation decisions entirely to individual residents
Wait until landfall to decide on evacuations
Evacuate only offshore barrier islands, not the mainland

questions.scenario: It's June 1856 in Iowa City, and you stand beside your family's two-wheeled handcart, loaded with everything you own, about to set out for Salt Lake City instead of buying an ox-drawn wagon.
questions.prompt: Why did church leaders promote handcarts over traditional ox-wagons for this migration?
questions.butterflyEffect: The plan let poor converts travel cheaply, and most 1856 companies arrived safely. But the late-departing Willie and Martin handcart companies were caught by early snows in Wyoming that October, and the resulting deaths led the church to largely abandon handcarts for wagon trains afterward.

choices.text: They cost far less and let poor converts travel without expensive oxen
They could carry twice the cargo of a standard wagon
They moved faster than horse teams over mountain passes
Federal law required all migrants to use handcarts that year

questions.prompt: Where did Kingsford Smith and his crew land to complete the first transpacific flight?
questions.butterflyEffect: The Southern Cross touched down at Eagle Farm, Brisbane, before a crowd of thousands, turning Kingsford Smith into a national hero overnight. The flight proved sustained trans-Pacific air travel was achievable and helped spur development of commercial air routes linking Australia to the Americas.

Sydney
Perth

A fresh ceasefire in 1997 finally brought the party into negotiations, which produced the Good Friday Agreement in April 1998, transforming the region's political future.

questions.prompt: What ultimately silenced the Opportunity rover after this final transmission?
questions.butterflyEffect: Unable to recharge its batteries in the storm's darkness, Opportunity never woke again. NASA made hundreds of recovery attempts before formally ending the mission in February 2019, closing out a rover that had outlasted its 90-sol design life by more than fourteen years.

questions.scenario: It is the afternoon of 6 August 2013 in a residential block of Rosario, Argentina. A gas leak has just triggered an explosion that collapsed one building outright, and rescue teams can see cracks spreading through the walls of the structures next door.

questions.prompt: What happened to the helicopter as it moved into the valley?
questions.butterflyEffect: The Chinook, callsign Extortion 17, was struck by a rocket-propelled grenade and crashed, killing all 38 aboard, including 17 Navy SEALs — the deadliest single loss of American life in the entire Afghan war. The disaster prompted a major review of how special operations quick-reaction forces were deployed into contested valleys.

questions.butterflyEffect: Residents who fled immediately to higher ground survived, while the flash floods and mudslides that followed damaged 71 towns and villages and killed at least 255 people. questions.butterflyEffect: The building endured fires, a tornado, and even battle damage, being rebuilt each time rather than abandoned. Restored to its early 18th-century form as part of the Colonial Williamsburg project, it survives today as the oldest college building in the United States.

choices.text: It burns down once and is never rebuilt
It survives repeated disasters through successive rebuildings and becomes the nation's oldest college building
It is torn down within a decade for a larger structure
It is converted into a private residence and loses its academic purpose

questions.scenario: It is August 1991, and you herd sheep on a Patagonian ranch as Chile's Hudson volcano begins erupting, sending thick ash drifting across the border into Argentina.
questions.prompt: What should you do to protect your flock as the ash keeps falling?
questions.butterflyEffect: The eruption was one of the largest of the 20th century, blanketing tens of thousands of square kilometres of Chile and Argentina in ash that killed livestock and smothered pastureland for years. Patagonian sheep farming suffered lasting damage, and the eruption remains a reference point for volcanic hazard studies in the southern Andes.

choices.text: Move the flock away from the ashfall zone as quickly as possible
Keep grazing as normal since volcanic ash poses no risk to animals
Wait for authorities to clear the ash before moving the sheep
Slaughter the entire flock immediately as a precaution

questions.prompt: What is the appropriate response as the agents present their warrant?
questions.butterflyEffect: The search recovered documents marked classified, later leading to federal charges against Donald Trump over the retention of national defense information—the first such indictment of a former U.S. president. The raid intensified political battles over the handling of presidential records and shaped the 2024 election cycle.

choices.text: Deny the agents entry until the former president personally authorizes it
Allow access and cooperate, as the warrant is legally binding
Alert news outlets before the agents can begin the search
Insist on renegotiating the scope of the warrant with the agents on site

questions.scenario: You are part of a maintenance crew working high on the Warsaw radio mast near Gąbin in August 1991, replacing tensioning cables on what is still the tallest structure ever built.
questions.prompt: What should you do when the mast begins to sway unexpectedly during the cable work?
questions.butterflyEffect: A tensioning error during that maintenance work caused the mast to buckle and collapse entirely, killing one worker. The structure was never rebuilt, ending its 17-year reign as the world's tallest building and marking the limits of that era's extreme-height mast engineering.

choices.text: Stop work immediately and evacuate down the mast
Keep working to finish the cable replacement before dark

questions.prompt: How did Iran respond diplomatically once it learned that personnel at its consulate had been killed during the takeover?
questions.butterflyEffect: Tehran accused the Taliban of murdering its diplomats, recalled its envoys, and moved substantial military forces to the Afghan border, bringing the two governments to the brink of war. The crisis deepened Iran's hostility toward the Taliban regime for years and hardened its support for opposing Afghan factions.

choices.text: Iran severed diplomatic engagement and mobilized troops along the Afghan border
Iran quickly recognized the new Taliban administration to preserve ties
Iran offered the Taliban economic aid to smooth over the incident
Iran remained silent on the matter to avoid regional tension

questions.scenario: It is September 1961. UN Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjöld is flying into the Congo Crisis to broker a ceasefire between UN forces and Katangan leader Moïse Tshombe, when his plane goes down near Ndola.
questions.prompt: After three official inquiries into the crash, what did investigators conclude?
questions.butterflyEffect: No inquiry ever conclusively determined the cause of the crash, leaving sabotage theories unresolved for decades. The UN later reopened investigations in the 2010s after new evidence surfaced, and Hammarskjöld's death remains one of the great unsolved mysteries of the Cold War, deepening suspicion around great-power interference in Congo's decolonization.

choices.text: Pilot error caused the crash, case closed definitively
The cause remained officially inconclusive despite years of investigation

A mechanical fault was proven beyond doubt

questions.scenario: It is September 1850 in Boston. Congress has just passed the Fugitive Slave Act, making it a federal crime to help an escaped enslaved person and requiring ordinary citizens, even in free states, to assist in their capture.
questions.prompt: As a Northern abolitionist, how do you respond to the new law?
questions.butterflyEffect: Many Northerners defied the law openly, forming vigilance committees and expanding the Underground Railroad, while some states passed personal liberty laws undermining it. The backlash helped inspire Harriet Beecher Stowe's 'Uncle Tom's Cabin' in 1852 and hardened sectional divisions that pushed the country toward civil war.

choices.text: Comply fully and report any fugitives you encounter
Join a vigilance committee to help fugitives escape further north
Move to the South to avoid the controversy
Petition Congress and wait quietly for repeal

questions.prompt: What ultimately became of Indianola in the years after this storm?
questions.butterflyEffect: The 1875 hurricane devastated the town and crippled its standing as a major Texas port, shifting trade toward Galveston and other harbors. A second catastrophic hurricane in 1886 finished what the first began, and Indianola was never rebuilt, becoming a ghost town remembered only through historical markers.

choices.text: The town rebuilt and became Texas's leading port
The town declined and was later destroyed for good by another hurricane in 1886

Residents relocated the entire town inland within a year

questions.prompt: What programming strategy did The CW adopt to define its identity?
questions.butterflyEffect: The CW built its brand around young-adult dramas like 'Supernatural' and 'Gilmore Girls,' later adding hits like 'Gossip Girl.' This niche identity sustained the network for years until financial pressures led Nexstar to acquire majority ownership in 2022 and pivot toward reality and sports programming.

questions.butterflyEffect: The investigation dragged on for years before focusing on Bruce Ivins, a U.S. Army biodefense scientist, who died by suicide in 2008 before any charges were filed. The case was formally closed in 2010, and the attacks spurred a major expansion of U.S. biodefense research funding and mail-screening security.

questions.prompt: What did UK party leaders offer in a last-minute push to keep wavering Scots voting No?
questions.butterflyEffect: The leaders of the three main UK parties signed 'The Vow,' promising greater devolved powers to the Scottish Parliament if Scotland stayed in the Union. This pledge helped secure the No victory and led to the Scotland Act 2016, though debates over its fulfillment fueled renewed independence campaigning after Brexit.

choices.text: A guarantee of a separate Scottish currency backed by the Bank of England
A promise of new powers for the Scottish Parliament, known as 'The Vow'

questions.scenario: It is 1138, and you advise the Emir of Shaizar, whose city has endured weeks of siege by the combined army of Byzantine Emperor John II Komnenos and the Crusader princes of Antioch and Tripoli. Food is running short and no relief force is coming.
questions.prompt: What should the Emir do to end the siege on the best terms available?
questions.butterflyEffect: The Emir bought off the siege with a large tribute and a nominal oath of vassalage to Byzantium. The uneasy Byzantine-Crusader alliance collapsed soon afterward over rival claims to Antioch, and Shaizar's Munqidhite rulers kept their effective independence for decades.

choices.text: Surrender unconditionally and abandon the city
Sue for terms and accept vassalage under Byzantine overlordship, paying tribute

questions.prompt: What does al-Asaad do when IS demands he disclose the hidden antiquities?
questions.butterflyEffect: Al-Asaad refused, and he was publicly killed by IS that August, becoming a global symbol of resistance to cultural destruction. IS went on to demolish the Temple of Baalshamin and the Temple of Bel, but much of Palmyra's movable heritage survived because its location was never revealed.

Refuse to cooperate despite the threat to his life

questions.prompt: What actually happened as the long siege reached its final weeks?
questions.butterflyEffect: No Byzantine fleet ever arrived, and Syracuse fell to the Aghlabids in May 878, ending centuries of Byzantine rule over the city. The loss accelerated the Muslim conquest of Sicily, though Byzantine forces held on around Taormina in the island's northeast for another generation.

choices.text: A relief fleet arrived just in time to break the siege
The city held out and negotiated favorable terms of surrender

The Aghlabids abandoned the siege due to disease in their camp

questions.prompt: What did Feld Entertainment cite as the deciding factor in ending the circus?
questions.butterflyEffect: Ticket sales fell sharply after elephants were retired from the show in 2016 amid animal-welfare pressure, and Feld Entertainment closed the circus in 2017 rather than keep running it at a loss. The brand didn't vanish for good: in 2023 Ringling relaunched as an animal-free touring show for a new generation.

A change in ownership that redirected the company toward film

questions.prompt: What do you do to bring Busoni's unfinished masterpiece to the stage?
questions.butterflyEffect: Jarnach completed the ending himself, and the opera premiered in Dresden in 1925, becoming the standard version performed for decades. choices.text: Complete the final scene using Busoni's sketches and stylistic voice

Rewrite the entire opera in your own style

questions.scenario: You are a parish priest in June 1966, reading a startling bulletin from Rome: the Vatican has just acted on the Index Librorum Prohibitorum, the list of forbidden books that has shaped Catholic reading for over four centuries.
questions.prompt: What did the Vatican do with the centuries-old Index of banned books?
questions.butterflyEffect: Pope Paul VI formally abolished the Index in 1966, ending its legal force though the Church still cautioned against works it once condemned. The move reflected the broader liberalization of Vatican II and gave Catholic readers and publishers far greater freedom.

questions.butterflyEffect: 2002 MN was only discovered three days after its closest approach, exposing serious gaps in the sky surveys meant to catch city-threatening asteroids before they arrive. questions.butterflyEffect: The "yes" vote won with about 55.5 percent, narrowly clearing the required threshold. Montenegro declared independence on June 3, 2006, becoming the last republic to emerge from the breakup of Yugoslavia, and went on to join NATO and pursue EU membership.

At least 55 percent of votes cast

questions.scenario: It is May 1864 near Spotsylvania Court House, Virginia. You serve under Ulysses S. Grant after ferocious fighting, including the brutal hand-to-hand combat at the "Bloody Angle," leaves both armies battered but neither broken.
questions.prompt: What does Grant do after this costly, inconclusive battle against Lee?
questions.butterflyEffect: Rather than retreat as previous Union commanders had after setbacks, Grant pressed on southward toward Richmond, famously vowing to "fight it out on this line." This relentless pressure defined the Overland Campaign, leading to Cold Harbor and the long siege of Petersburg, and ultimately ground down Lee's army over the war's final year.

Continue advancing south toward Richmond despite heavy losses

Hand over command of the army to Sherman

questions.scenario: It is May 21, 1991, in Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu. Former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi is campaigning for re-election when a young woman steps forward from the crowd to greet him, an explosive belt concealed beneath her clothes.

She detonates the explosive belt, killing Gandhi and herself
She hands him a garland and steps back safely
She is searched and found to be unarmed

questions.prompt: What happens to Defoe once he is revealed as the author?
questions.butterflyEffect: Defoe was arrested, pilloried, and imprisoned in Newgate for seditious libel, an ordeal that nearly ruined him financially but built his reputation as a fearless writer. He later turned to journalism and, in his fifties, to novels such as Robinson Crusoe, helping to establish the modern English novel.

He is arrested and imprisoned for seditious libel

questions.prompt: What do these wavering Saitō generals ultimately decide to do?
questions.butterflyEffect: They defected to Nobunaga, fatally weakening the castle's defenses from within. Nobunaga captured Inabayama, renamed the town Gifu, and made it his base for the campaigns that would carry him toward unifying Japan.

Fight to the death defending Tatsuoki

questions.scenario: It's September 13, 1848, near Cavendish, Vermont. An accidental explosion has just driven a 13-pound iron tamping rod clean through railroad foreman Phineas Gage's skull, and as the attending physician you must decide how to treat him.
questions.prompt: What did Dr. John Harlow actually do to treat Gage's wound?
questions.butterflyEffect: Harlow's conservative treatment let Gage survive, but his altered temperament afterward became one of the earliest documented links between the frontal lobe and personality. The case still anchors neuroscience discussions of brain injury and behavior today.

Clean the wound, remove loose bone fragments, and let it drain while watching for infection
Perform immediate exploratory brain surgery

questions.prompt: What should the crew do once they lose visual reference and become spatially disoriented?
questions.butterflyEffect: Instead of climbing away, the crew disengaged the autopilot and lost control in the dark, killing all 88 aboard, including a former Russian general. Disengage the autopilot and fly by feel toward the runway lights
Continue the descent at the same rate
Radio the tower and wait for further instructions before acting

questions.prompt: What did Saudi Arabia do to offset the sudden loss of production?
questions.butterflyEffect: Aramco drew on strategic reserves and repaired facilities faster than expected, restoring output within weeks, but oil prices still posted their biggest single-day jump in decades. questions.scenario: You're at Cindy Campbell's back-to-school party in the rec room at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue in the Bronx, August 1973. Her brother Clive spins funk records, but dancers keep drifting off the floor whenever a song shifts into vocals.

questions.butterflyEffect: Clive Campbell, soon known as DJ Kool Herc, used two copies of the same record to loop and extend the instrumental drum "break," and began chanting over it to the crowd. This breakbeat technique and his rhythmic call-outs became the foundations of DJing and rapping, and the Bronx party is now regarded as hip-hop's birthplace.

Play each song straight through without any interruption

questions.butterflyEffect: The Montreal Protocol committed nations to phasing out CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances, and every UN member state eventually ratified it. questions.butterflyEffect: Seeding Esther with silver iodide appeared to cause some structural changes in the storm, encouraging the Weather Bureau to expand cloud-seeding experiments into the later Project Stormfury program. questions.butterflyEffect: The UK withdrew the pound from the Exchange Rate Mechanism entirely, letting it float freely and devalue. questions.prompt: What is the correct duty of an imperial astronomer confronted with this new 'guest star'?

questions.butterflyEffect: Bernon Mitchell and William Martin resurfaced in Moscow that September, publicly defecting and exposing details of NSA's signals intelligence operations against the Soviet Union. Defected to the Soviet Union and revealed NSA secrets

questions.butterflyEffect: The warning was lifted roughly half an hour after being issued, just before waves several metres high struck Palu's coast, catching many who had gone back to low ground. Combined with catastrophic soil liquefaction that swallowed neighborhoods like Petobo and Balaroa, the disaster forced a rework of Indonesia's tsunami-warning system and evacuation procedures.

choices.text: Move to higher ground regardless of the warning being lifted
Return home since the official warning has ended
Gather on the beach to watch for waves
Wait for a second earthquake before deciding

questions.scenario: It is 28 September 1106 near Tinchebray in Normandy. You ride with Duke Robert Curthose's knights as King Henry I's English and Norman forces close in for a decisive clash between the sons of William the Conqueror.
questions.prompt: What happened to Duke Robert Curthose after the battle?
questions.butterflyEffect: Henry's decisive victory reunited England and Normandy under one ruler for the first time since the Conqueror's death, while Robert spent nearly three decades as a prisoner until his death in 1134. The battle cemented Henry's control of his father's cross-Channel realm and shaped Anglo-Norman politics for generations.

choices.text: He was captured and imprisoned by Henry for the rest of his life
He escaped to rally fresh forces in Normandy
He was killed on the battlefield
He negotiated a truce and kept his dukedom

questions.scenario: It is 28 September 351 on the plains near Mursa in Pannonia. You stand among Constantius II's eastern legions facing the army of the usurper Magnentius, whose seizure of the western throne has plunged the empire into civil war.
questions.prompt: What was the outcome of this clash for Magnentius?
questions.butterflyEffect: Mursa Major was among the bloodiest battles of the age, gutting the field armies of both sides. Magnentius escaped the field but never recovered, taking his own life in 353 after further defeat, leaving Constantius sole emperor but commanding legions too weakened to easily face renewed threats from Persia and the Germanic frontier.

choices.text: His forces were decisively defeated, and he later took his own life
He won a clear victory and secured the western empire
The battle ended in stalemate and years of further siege
He was captured and executed on the field

questions.prompt: What happens when you attempt to storm Montreal with your undersized force?
questions.butterflyEffect: British regulars and Canadian militia surrounded and captured Ethan Allen's party at Longue-Pointe. Allen was shipped to England as a prisoner, and the failed raid signaled that Canadians would not rally to the American cause, weakening the broader invasion of Canada.

choices.text: You are surrounded and forced to surrender to British and Canadian militia
You successfully seize Montreal and hold it for the Continental Congress
You retreat safely back to Fort Ticonderoga
You link up with Benedict Arnold's column to besiege Quebec together

questions.scenario: You are a mission engineer at JPL watching the Titan rocket carry the Mars Observer spacecraft skyward, the first American mission to Mars in nearly two decades.
questions.prompt: What happens to Mars Observer eleven months later, as it nears the planet?
questions.butterflyEffect: Contact with Mars Observer was lost on 21 August 1993, just before it was to fire its engines and enter orbit, likely due to a fuel line rupture. The costly failure pushed NASA toward its "faster, better, cheaper" strategy, leading to smaller, more frequent Mars missions like Global Surveyor and Pathfinder.

choices.text: Contact with the spacecraft is lost just before orbit insertion, and the mission is declared lost
It enters Mars orbit successfully and begins years of mapping
It crash-lands intact on the Martian surface and keeps transmitting
Ground controllers redirect it to fly past an asteroid instead

questions.scenario: You are an officer in the Yemeni army in September 1962, days after Imam Muhammad al-Badr's coronation, as Abdullah al-Sallal moves troops toward the palace to declare a republic.
questions.prompt: Do you join al-Sallal's coup against the newly crowned Imam?
questions.butterflyEffect: Al-Sallal's forces dethroned al-Badr, who escaped to the Saudi border and rallied northern tribes to fight back, igniting a full civil war that lasted until 1970. Egypt backed the republicans and Saudi Arabia the royalists, turning Yemen into an early proxy battleground of the wider Arab Cold War.

choices.text: Join al-Sallal's revolutionaries and help declare Yemen a republic
Stay loyal to Imam al-Badr and defend the palace
Flee immediately to Saudi Arabia to avoid taking sides
Broker a power-sharing deal between the army and the imamate

questions.prompt: Do you launch an immediate cavalry charge against the Ottoman position?
questions.butterflyEffect: The French knights charged ahead of the main army, broke through the first Ottoman line, then were encircled and cut down when Ottoman reserves and cavalry closed in. The crusader defeat ended the campaign, cemented Ottoman power in the Balkans for generations, and left many captured nobles to be ransomed at great cost.

choices.text: Charge immediately, ignoring Hungarian warnings to wait
Wait for Sigismund's Hungarian troops to advance together

Send envoys to negotiate a truce with Bayezid I

questions.scenario: It is September 1981, and you sit in the U.S. Senate chamber as President Reagan's nominee, Arizona judge Sandra Day O'Connor, awaits the final vote to become the first woman on the Supreme Court.
questions.prompt: How does the Senate vote on confirming O'Connor?
questions.butterflyEffect: The Senate confirmed O'Connor unanimously, 99–0, making her the first woman to sit on the Supreme Court. She became a decisive swing vote for 25 years on issues from abortion to affirmative action before retiring in 2006.

They reject her over concerns about abortion rulings

questions.scenario: It is August 1487, and you serve as an advisor to Ferdinand and Isabella outside the walls of Málaga. The city has held out for four grueling months against the royal siege, draining the Crown's treasury and patience, before finally offering to surrender.
questions.prompt: What terms do the Catholic Monarchs impose on Málaga after its prolonged resistance?
questions.butterflyEffect: Because the city had resisted so long and cost the Crown so dearly, most of Málaga's population was enslaved rather than shown the mercy earlier cities received. The harshness became a cautionary example, and it influenced Granada's decision in 1492 to negotiate surrender quickly rather than risk a similar siege.

choices.text: Free passage and mercy for all inhabitants
A heavy ransom in exchange for freedom
Mass enslavement as punishment for the long resistance
Immediate expulsion but retention of property

questions.prompt: Facing near-certain impeachment, what does Musharraf ultimately choose to do?
questions.butterflyEffect: On 18 August 2008, Musharraf resigned rather than face a parliamentary vote, ending nearly nine years in power that began with his 1999 coup. Asif Ali Zardari was elected president weeks later, and Pakistan entered a period of fragile civilian-led governance under continued military influence.

choices.text: Resign the presidency before the vote
Declare martial law to block the vote

questions.prompt: What immediate consequence followed this ambush for France's role in the war?
questions.butterflyEffect: Ten French soldiers were killed, France's deadliest single engagement in decades, and it triggered fierce debate at home over the country's deepening commitment in Afghanistan. President Sarkozy visited the site personally, and the ambush became a lasting symbol of the war's cost for French public opinion.

questions.scenario: You are an assistant at the US Naval Observatory in Washington in mid-August 1877, watching Asaph Hall painstakingly search the glare around Mars during its close opposition, having already spotted one faint moon days earlier.
questions.prompt: What does Hall discover just days after finding Mars's outer moon, Deimos?
questions.butterflyEffect: Hall discovered Phobos, the larger and closer of Mars's two tiny moons, completing the pair he named for the sons of Ares who personified fear and panic. The discovery reshaped understanding of Mars's system and, over a century later, Phobos's rapidly decaying orbit became a key data point for planning future Mars missions.

choices.text: A second, inner moon of Mars: Phobos
A ring system around Mars

questions.scenario: It is the morning of 27 May 1941. You are aboard HMS Rodney, closing on the crippled German battleship Bismarck, which can barely steer after a rudder hit the night before.
questions.prompt: What does the British fleet do to finish off the wounded Bismarck?
questions.butterflyEffect: Rodney and King George V pounded Bismarck with gunfire at close range, and cruiser Dorsetshire finished her with torpedoes; the crew also opened scuttling valves as she went down. Her loss ended Hitler's hopes of using surface raiders against Atlantic convoys, pushing the Kriegsmarine toward a U-boat-centered strategy for the rest of the war.

choices.text: Close in with concentrated gunfire and torpedoes until she sinks

Withdraw the fleet, having already crippled her enough

questions.prompt: What does this record, The Freewheelin' Bob Dylan, go on to do for him?
questions.butterflyEffect: The album, featuring "Blowin' in the Wind" and "A Hard Rain's A-Gonna Fall," established Dylan almost overnight as the defining songwriter of the American protest and civil rights movement. questions.prompt: What happens to the ship in the minutes that follow?
questions.butterflyEffect: Princess Irene exploded catastrophically while the mines were still being loaded, sinking almost instantly with the loss of 352 lives, including many dockyard workers. The inquiry pointed to faulty handling of primers and detonators, and the Admiralty tightened procedures for arming mines aboard ship afterward.

The mines are found defective and removed before any harm is done

questions.prompt: What happens as the horse refuses the jump?
questions.butterflyEffect: Reeve was thrown headfirst over the horse's neck, shattering his upper spine and leaving him paralyzed from the neck down. questions.prompt: How do you arm this new interceptor, the future F-4 Phantom II?

questions.prompt: What should you do to survive until a rescue team can reach you?

U.S. Marines executed a daring extraction under fire, and O'Grady's survival story became a major morale boost, later told in his own bestselling memoir.
